pair.linkWithCode: WhatsApp is on this phone? Link with a code instead
pair.codeStep1: Open WhatsApp → Settings → Linked Devices → Link a Device
pair.title: Link your WhatsApp
pair.bridgeNotResponding: The WhatsApp bridge is running but not responding.
pair.bridgeNotRunning: The WhatsApp bridge container isn't running yet.
pair.scanIntro: Scan this with your phone — Yorik becomes a linked device, just like WhatsApp Web.
pair.installDocker: Install Docker Desktop (or the Docker Engine + Compose plugin on Linux), then refresh this page.
pair.firstStartHint: First-time start downloads the bridge image — can take a minute or two. The QR will appear here automatically when the bridge is ready.
pair.restartHint: Will restart the existing container (~5 sec). Usually fixes a wedged bridge.
pair.startHint: Will run `docker compose up -d whatsapp-bridge` for you. First start can take 1–2 minutes while the image builds.
pair.timeout: WhatsApp didn't start within 3 minutes. Try again; if it keeps failing, an admin can look under Settings → System.

import.title: Import WhatsApp chat history
import.intro: On your phone: open a chat → menu → More → Export Chat → Without Media. Save the .txt or .zip here.

disconnect.title: Disconnect WhatsApp?
disconnect.intro: Currently connected as {{name}}. Your phone's "Linked Devices" list will lose this connection. A fresh QR will appear so you can pair a different account.
disconnect.wipeLabel: Also delete all message history from Yorik
disconnect.wipeHint: By default, conversations stay archived locally — only the connection is reset. Check this only if you want a completely clean slate.
disconnect.partialFailed: Disconnect partially failed: {{error}}. You may need to reload the page.

contact.confirmSpam: Mark "{{name}}" as spam? Future WhatsApp messages from this number will be tagged spam.
contact.pending: {{name}} is a pending contact — confirm to add to your address book.
contact.unknownNumber: This number isn't in your contacts yet.
